metaTitle: Cert IV in Plumbing & Services Fast Track RPL (CPC40920)
metaDescription: Turn your plumbing experience into a CPC40920 Cert IV in Plumbing and Services through RPL. Online assessment, Australia-wide. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: Already running jobs, supervising apprentices or designing hydraulic systems? The CPC40920 Certificate IV in Plumbing and Services through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) turns that experience into a nationally recognised qualification, without going back to the classroom. You build your evidence online, and a registered training organisation assesses it.
whoIsItFor:
This qualification suits experienced plumbers who are ready to step up from the tools into supervision, contracting or design. It is the next level after the Certificate III in Plumbing, and in several states it is the qualification behind higher-level plumbing licences.

  • Licensed or registered plumbers who want to run their own plumbing business
  • Leading hands and site supervisors on residential or commercial jobs
  • Plumbers who quote, plan and manage jobs and sign off compliance
  • Hydraulic designers and drafters working on water, sanitary, drainage or gas systems

Most successful RPL candidates have several years of work as a qualified plumber, including time planning work, reading plans and specifications, and dealing with clients and regulators. For the operations stream you need to hold a Certificate III in Plumbing or be authorised to do plumbing work by an Australian regulator.
evidenceExamples:
The assessor needs to see that you work at Certificate IV level: planning, supervising and taking responsibility for compliance, not only doing the work. Useful evidence includes:

  • Your plumbing licence or registration, and your Certificate III (or overseas equivalent)
  • Quotes, estimates and job costings you have prepared
  • Plans, hydraulic drawings or designs you have read, marked up or produced
  • Compliance certificates and certificates of compliance you have lodged
  • Photos and short videos of completed jobs, with a note of your role
  • Toolbox talks, site inductions or safety documents you have run
  • A reference from an employer, builder or client describing your supervisory duties
  • Business records if you are self-employed: ABN, invoices, insurance

Don't worry if your paperwork is patchy. Our team helps you work out what you already have and what is worth collecting before you submit.
licensingInfo:
Plumbing licences are issued by each state and territory regulator, not by training organisations. The Certificate IV is commonly the education requirement for higher-level licences, such as a plumbing contractor, master plumber or supervisor licence, and for hydraulic design work. The details differ by state:

  • Queensland: plumbing and drainage licences are issued by the QBCC.
  • New South Wales: licences and certificates are issued by NSW Fair Trading.
  • Victoria: plumbers are registered and licensed by the Building and Plumbing Commission (formerly the VBA).
  • Other states and territories: each has its own plumbing regulator and licence classes.

RPL gives you the qualification. The licence is a separate application to your regulator, which may ask for extra experience, exams or units. Tell us your state and the licence you're aiming for, and we'll check the qualification and electives match it before you start.
description:
The CPC40920 Certificate IV in Plumbing and Services is the advanced plumbing qualification in Australia. It covers the skills of a plumbing service operator who runs jobs, supervises others and takes responsibility for design and compliance, as well as the hydraulic consultant who designs water, sanitary, drainage and gas systems for homes, commercial buildings and industry.

There are two pathways: the operations stream for working plumbers moving into contracting and supervision, and the hydraulic services design stream for people who design systems. Through RPL, the electives are matched to the work you actually do.
imageAlt: Experienced plumber reviewing hydraulic plans on a job site

faqs.q: Can I get the CPC40920 Certificate IV in Plumbing and Services through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes. If you are already working as a plumber and have experience planning jobs, supervising work, estimating or designing systems, you can have that experience assessed through RPL. You don't sit in a classroom; an assessor reviews your evidence and confirms the units you're competent in.

faqs.q: How long does Cert IV Plumbing RPL take?
faqs.a: Most people finish within 4 to 12 weeks. The biggest factor is how quickly you gather your evidence. If you already have photos, quotes, compliance certificates and a reference ready, it can be faster.

faqs.q: Do I need a Certificate III in Plumbing first?
faqs.a: For the operations stream, yes: you need the Certificate III in Plumbing or authorisation from an Australian plumbing regulator. The hydraulic services design stream has no entry requirement. If you don't hold the Cert III yet, look at CPC32420 Certificate III in Plumbing through RPL first.

faqs.q: Can I do it 100% online?
faqs.a: The evidence is collected and submitted online, and interviews are done by phone or video, so you can do it from anywhere in Australia. In some cases the assessor may ask for a short practical observation or a video of you working.

faqs.q: What does RPL for Cert IV Plumbing cost?
faqs.a: The cost depends on the stream, how many units you can show evidence for and whether any gap training is needed. RPL is usually much cheaper and faster than studying the full course, because you only pay to be assessed on what you already know. Start with a free eligibility check and we'll give you a clear quote.

faqs.q: Does the Cert IV get me a plumbing contractor or master plumber licence?
faqs.a: It is a key requirement for higher-level licences in several states, but the licence itself comes from your state regulator, which may have extra requirements such as experience or exams. Tell us which state and licence you're after and we'll make sure the electives line up.

faqs.q: Is an RPL Certificate IV the same as one from full study?
faqs.a: Yes. It is the same nationally recognised qualification, issued by a registered training organisation. Your certificate doesn't say whether you got it through RPL or by studying.

metaTitle: Plumbing RPL: Cert III Fast Track Online (CPC32420)
metaDescription: Worked as a plumber without the paperwork? Get your CPC32420 Cert III in Plumbing through RPL, a step to your licence. Online. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: If you have years of plumbing work behind you but no Australian trade certificate, the CPC32420 Certificate III in Plumbing through RPL is the quickest way to get it. Your on-the-job experience is assessed against the national standard, so you skip the units you can already do.
whoIsItFor:
The Certificate III is the trade qualification for plumbers in Australia and the usual starting point for a plumbing licence. RPL suits people who already do the work:

  • Plumbers who trained on the job but never finished an apprenticeship
  • Plumbers' labourers and trade assistants with long, broad experience
  • Overseas-qualified plumbers who need an Australian qualification
  • Apprentices who left before completing and kept working in the trade
  • Drainers, gasfitters and roof plumbers who want the full trade qualification

The qualification covers a wide range of plumbing work: water services, sanitary, drainage, roofing, and gas and mechanical services depending on electives. Candidates usually have several years of hands-on plumbing across most of these areas.
evidenceExamples:
For a trade qualification, the assessor wants to see the range and quality of your work. Strong evidence includes:

  • Photos and videos of your work at each stage: rough-in, fit-off, drainage, hot water, gas or roofing
  • Payslips, group certificates or a statement of service showing time in the trade
  • A detailed reference from a licensed plumber who has supervised you
  • Any licences, tickets or permits you hold (White Card, confined space, working at heights)
  • Job sheets, invoices or compliance paperwork you have worked on
  • Overseas trade certificates, with translations if needed

You will also usually have a competency conversation with the assessor and a practical observation, which can be on site or by video.
licensingInfo:
Plumbing is licensed work in every Australian state and territory. The Certificate III in Plumbing is the base qualification regulators look for, but each regulator sets its own rules for licence classes such as water supply, sanitary, drainage and gasfitting.

  • Queensland: QBCC plumbing and drainage licences.
  • New South Wales: NSW Fair Trading tradesperson certificates and contractor licences.
  • Victoria: registration and licensing through the Building and Plumbing Commission (formerly the VBA).
  • WA, SA, TAS, ACT and NT: each has its own plumbing licensing body.

Your electives decide which licence classes the qualification supports. Tell us your state and the work you do (for example gasfitting), and we'll make sure the right units are included.
description:
The CPC32420 Certificate III in Plumbing is the national trade qualification for plumbers. It covers installing and maintaining water services, sanitary plumbing and drainage, and, depending on the electives chosen, roof plumbing, gas services and mechanical services in homes and commercial buildings.

It is a large qualification with a strong core, so RPL is assessed against real work across these areas. Once complete, it opens the door to a plumbing licence and to the Certificate IV in Plumbing and Services.
imageAlt: Plumber installing copper pipework in a residential bathroom

faqs.q: Can I get a Certificate III in Plumbing through RPL without an apprenticeship?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have enough real plumbing experience. RPL assesses what you already do on the job against the national standard. You'll need solid evidence across the core areas of the trade, such as water services, sanitary and drainage.

faqs.q: How long does Cert III Plumbing RPL take?
faqs.a: Usually 6 to 12 weeks. It's longer than smaller qualifications because the Cert III has a large core and a practical assessment. Having your photos, references and service history ready speeds it up.

faqs.q: Do I need a practical assessment?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Plumbing is a hands-on trade, so the assessor will want to see you work. This can be an on-site observation or a recorded video, depending on the assessing organisation and your location.

faqs.q: I trained as a plumber overseas. Does my experience count?
faqs.a: It can. Overseas experience and qualifications are assessed the same way as Australian experience, against the national units. Translated certificates, references and photos of your work all help.

faqs.q: What does RPL for Cert III Plumbing cost?
faqs.a: It depends on how much of the qualification your evidence covers, the electives you need and whether any gap training is required. RPL is generally far cheaper than a four-year apprenticeship or full-time study. Start with a free eligibility check for a clear quote.

faqs.q: Will this get me a plumbing licence?
faqs.a: The Certificate III is the core qualification for a plumbing licence, but the licence is issued by your state regulator, which may require extra steps such as supervised experience or exams. We help you choose electives that match the licence you want.

faqs.q: Is the RPL certificate the same as finishing an apprenticeship?
faqs.a: The qualification is the same nationally recognised CPC32420, issued by a registered training organisation. The certificate doesn't show that it was gained through RPL.

metaTitle: Cert III Carpentry Fast Track RPL Online (CPC30326)
metaDescription: Fast track your CPC30326 Cert III in Carpentry (replaces CPC30220) with RPL. Use your building experience, assessed online. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The CPC30326 Certificate III in Carpentry is the current carpentry trade qualification, replacing CPC30220. If you've been framing, fitting out or doing formwork for years, RPL turns that experience into your trade certificate, assessed against your real work rather than classroom hours.
whoIsItFor:
RPL for carpentry is for people already working in the trade who don't have the paper to prove it:

  • Carpenters who learned on the job without finishing an apprenticeship
  • Formworkers, framers and fit-out carpenters
  • Builders' labourers with long carpentry experience
  • Overseas-trained carpenters who need an Australian qualification
  • Carpenters planning to move up to a builder's licence

Most candidates have at least 3–4 years of carpentry work across a range of tasks: setting out, floor and wall framing, roof framing, windows and doors, and fixing.
evidenceExamples:
Carpentry RPL relies on showing the range of work you've done. Good evidence includes:

  • Photos and videos of your work at each stage: set-out, frames, trusses, roofs, stairs, fit-off
  • A reference from a builder or licensed carpenter who has supervised you
  • Payslips, a statement of service or ABN invoices that show time in the trade
  • Your White Card and any other tickets (working at heights, EWP, scaffolding)
  • Plans or cutting lists you have worked from
  • Overseas trade certificates, if you have them

The assessor will usually also talk you through your work and arrange a practical observation, either on site or by video.
licensingInfo:
Carpentry licensing depends on your state. In some states you need a licence to contract for carpentry work above a set value, and the Certificate III is the qualification regulators expect. Examples:

  • New South Wales: a carpentry contractor licence or qualified supervisor certificate from NSW Fair Trading.
  • Queensland: a QBCC carpentry trade contractor licence.
  • Victoria and other states: carpenters working under a registered builder may not need their own licence, but the qualification is often required by employers.

Want your own builder's licence later? The Cert III is the stepping stone to the CPC40120 Certificate IV in Building and Construction.
description:
The CPC30326 Certificate III in Carpentry covers the work of a carpenter in residential and commercial construction: setting out, building floor, wall and roof frames, installing windows, doors and stairs, formwork and general fixing. It replaces CPC30220 from the latest construction training package release.

The qualification has a large core plus specialist electives, so through RPL your evidence is mapped to the work you actually do, whether that's house framing, commercial formwork or fit-out.
imageAlt: Carpenter building timber wall frames on a residential site

faqs.q: What replaced CPC30220 Certificate III in Carpentry?
faqs.a: CPC30220 has been superseded by CPC30326 Certificate III in Carpentry, the current version. New enrolments, including RPL, are in the current version. If you already hold CPC30220, it remains a valid qualification.

faqs.q: Can I get my carpentry trade certificate through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have enough carpentry experience. An assessor checks your evidence, such as photos, references and a practical observation, against each unit. You only do training for any gaps.

faqs.q: How long does carpentry RPL take?
faqs.a: Usually 6 to 12 weeks, depending on how fast you collect evidence and book the practical assessment. Having photos and a builder's reference ready makes a big difference.

faqs.q: Can I do carpentry RPL online?
faqs.a: The paperwork, uploads and interview are all online. Because carpentry is practical, there's usually a practical observation, which may be done on your work site or by video.

faqs.q: What does carpentry RPL cost?
faqs.a: The price depends on how much of the qualification your evidence covers and whether any gap training is needed. It's usually much less than a full apprenticeship or TAFE course. A free eligibility check gives you a clear quote.

faqs.q: I worked as a carpenter overseas. Can I still apply?
faqs.a: Yes. Overseas carpentry experience can count. You'll need evidence such as references, photos of your work and any trade certificates, translated if needed.

metaTitle: Cert IV Building & Construction Fast Track RPL (CPC40120)
metaDescription: Fast track your CPC40120 Cert IV in Building and Construction with RPL, the qualification behind most builder licences. 100% online. Free check.
heroIntro: The CPC40120 Certificate IV in Building and Construction is the qualification behind a builder's licence in most states. If you're already running jobs, supervising trades or managing small builds, RPL lets you have that experience assessed online instead of studying for a year or more.
whoIsItFor:
This qualification is for people who already manage building work and want the qualification to match:

  • Carpenters and other tradespeople running residential jobs
  • Site supervisors, foremen and leading hands
  • Project coordinators and contract administrators on low-rise builds
  • Tradies who want to apply for a builder's licence or registration
  • Overseas builders working in Australian construction

Successful candidates usually have several years in construction with real responsibility: reading plans, scheduling trades, estimating, ordering materials and keeping the site compliant and safe.
evidenceExamples:
The assessor needs to see you manage building work, not only do it. Useful evidence includes:

  • Quotes, estimates and cost plans you have prepared
  • Construction schedules, programs and trade bookings
  • Plans and specifications you've worked from, with your notes
  • Site safety documents: SWMS, inductions, risk assessments
  • Building contracts, variations and client correspondence

licensingInfo:
Builder licences and registrations are issued by state and territory regulators. The Certificate IV in Building and Construction is usually the education requirement, alongside proof of experience and sometimes an exam. Examples:

  • New South Wales: a contractor licence (general builder) from NSW Fair Trading.
  • Queensland: a QBCC builder licence (for example Builder Low Rise).
  • Victoria: registration as a domestic builder with the Building and Plumbing Commission (formerly the VBA).
  • Other states: each regulator sets its own classes and requirements.

Some regulators require particular units. Tell us your state and the licence class you're after, and we'll check that the electives match before you start. For medium-rise or commercial work, see the CPC50220 Diploma of Building and Construction.
description:
The CPC40120 Certificate IV in Building and Construction covers the skills to plan, manage and supervise residential and small commercial building projects: estimating, contracts, building codes and standards, work health and safety, structural principles, and running a building site.

It has a building stream and a site management stream. Through RPL, the electives are chosen to match your role and, where relevant, your state's licensing requirements.
imageAlt: Builder reviewing construction plans with a tradesperson on site

faqs.q: Can I get the Cert IV in Building and Construction through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes. If you've been managing or supervising building work, such as quoting, scheduling, coordinating trades and handling compliance, you can have that experience assessed through RPL instead of studying the full course.

faqs.q: How long does Cert IV Building RPL take?
faqs.a: Most candidates finish in 6 to 12 weeks. Builders who already have quotes, contracts, schedules and photos of past projects tend to finish faster.

faqs.q: Will the Cert IV get me a builder's licence?
faqs.a: It is the main education requirement for a builder's licence in most states, but the licence comes from your state regulator, which also checks your experience and may require an exam. We'll check the electives suit your state before you start.

faqs.q: Do I need a trade qualification first?
faqs.a: The CPC40120 has no formal entry requirement, but you'll need real construction management experience for RPL. Many candidates are carpenters or other tradespeople who have moved into running jobs.

faqs.q: What does Cert IV Building RPL cost?
faqs.a: The cost depends on your evidence, the stream and electives, and whether any gap training is needed. RPL usually costs much less than studying the full qualification. Get a free eligibility check for a clear quote.

faqs.q: Can I do it 100% online?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. Your evidence is uploaded online and the competency conversation is by phone or video, from anywhere in Australia.

metaTitle: CPC30426 Cert III in Demolition RPL — Fast Track
metaDescription: Experienced demolition worker? Get the CPC30426 Certificate III in Demolition through RPL using your site experience. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The CPC30426 Certificate III in Demolition is the trade qualification for demolition workers. If you already strip out and demolish buildings and structures, RPL recognises your experience so you get the qualification without going back to the classroom.
whoIsItFor:
• Demolition labourers and leading hands
  • Strip-out and soft demolition workers

evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of demolition and strip-out jobs you've worked on
  • Safe work method statements (SWMS) and job safety analyses you've used
  • Tickets and licences, such as the White Card, working at heights, hot work, EWP or asbestos awareness
  • A statement of service or reference from a demolition contractor
  • Payslips or employment records showing time in demolition roles
licensingInfo:
Demolition work is regulated by each state, and the rules depend on the type and size of the job. Licensing usually applies to the business or supervisor rather than to every worker. For example, in Queensland the QBCC licenses demolition work, in NSW higher-risk demolition needs a SafeWork NSW licence, and in Victoria demolishers register with the building regulator. Asbestos removal always needs a separate licence.

A qualification on its own is not a licence. Check your state's rules before you take on demolition work under your own name.
description:
The CPC30426 Certificate III in Demolition covers the skills of a qualified demolition worker: identifying hazards on demolition sites and managing risk, reading demolition site plans, selecting and using hand tools, small plant and hot work equipment, demolishing small buildings and structures, working safely at heights and handling dangerous goods and hazardous substances.

It replaces CPC30420, and electives can cover areas such as plant operation, rigging and strip-out work.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate III in Demolition through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have solid demolition experience. Photos of your jobs, SWMS, tickets and a reference from a demolition contractor are assessed against the units, with practical tasks observed where needed.

faqs.q: How long does it take?
faqs.a: Usually 6 to 12 weeks, depending on your evidence and when practical assessments can be arranged.

faqs.q: Does this qualification give me a demolition licence?
faqs.a: No. Licensing is handled by your state regulator and usually applies to the business or supervisor. The qualification is often part of what regulators look for, and the Certificate IV in Demolition is the supervisor-level qualification.

faqs.q: What does it cost?
faqs.a: The cost depends on how much your evidence covers and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.

faqs.q: I studied CPC30420. Do I need CPC30426?
faqs.a: No. CPC30420 remains valid if you completed it. New enrolments and RPL use the current CPC30426.
